sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The latest available arXiv announcement batch is 2026-11-04. Eight relevant papers span single-cell perturbation prediction, protein modeling, gene-expression noise, tumor and reaction-network theory, and medical physics. Attention evidence is sparse; this is a relevance-ranked selection, not an official popularity chart, and arXiv biomedical coverage is incomplete.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred relevance ranking is based on a limited arXiv category corpus, which does not represent biomedical research as a whole and omits much of bioRxiv and medRxiv.

sections.title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
sections.abstract: CellCanon combines single-cell expression prediction, source-grounded explanations, and observation-driven updating; on 339 held-out SciPlex3 drug–cell conditions across three cell lines, the authors report improved differential-expression metrics over their best baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report DE AUPRC and Macro-F1 gains of 63.3% and 17.3% over the best baseline, respectively, plus updating from simulated feedback using measurements withheld from the same dataset.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is on SciPlex3 and simulated measurement feedback, not prospective experiments or an external perturbation cohort; benchmark gains do not establish biological or clinical validity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct single-cell perturbation relevance; the abstract reports 339 held-out conditions in three cell lines and benchmark comparisons.

sections.title: Discrete Backbone Elasticity and Curvature-Dependent Torsion Statistics in Proteins
sections.abstract: The paper derives a local elastic statistical model linking neighboring protein-backbone bends to torsion distributions and tests it against protein structures and molecular-dynamics trajectories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the six-parameter baseline lowers negative log-density loss from 1.490 to 1.160 nats and improves torsion-sign and helix-fraction errors; a two-state extension further lowers test loss to 0.790 nats.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are statistical predictions against structural and simulation references, not experimental validation of folding or conformational kinetics. The discussion notes force-field and starting-state dependence and remaining errors associated with atomic context.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Model fitting on 194 ATLAS chains, testing on 1,744 sequence-nonredundant proteins, and transfer checks on 72 peptide/miniprotein trajectories.

sections.title: Experimental Assessment of Prompt Gamma Time Imaging in Complex Anatomy
sections.abstract: Prompt-Gamma Time Imaging jointly reconstructs proton velocity and gamma-emission profiles from multi-detector time-of-flight data, tested experimentally in an anthropomorphic head phantom.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report recovering material sequence and proton range from the phantom measurements, extending prompt-gamma timing beyond indirect range verification.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a phantom demonstration in two configurations, not patient testing. The paper notes limited sensitivity for materials with similar densities and material misclassification in some bins.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Eight detector modules; 100 MeV protons in two anatomical phantom configurations; approximately 1 mm range difference in the reported example.

sections.title: Modeling Gene Expression Noise: From Transcriptional Dynamics to Cell Growth and Division
sections.abstract: This review synthesizes stochastic gene-expression models that account for cell growth, DNA replication, cell-cycle variation, and division, including how these processes affect single-cell measurements and parameter inference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that static-cell telegraph/bursty models can misattribute noise when growth and division matter, and outline cell-cycle-resolved measurements and models needed for better inference.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a review, not a new experimental dataset or systematic evidence appraisal; its conclusions depend on the underlying studies and their measurement designs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The review covers modeling assumptions, inference strategies, and explicit open questions about cell-cycle-aware single-cell measurements.

sections.title: System-Theoretic Analysis of Extended Cellular Potts Models for Tumor Invasion
sections.abstract: The authors formulate an extended Cellular Potts model coupling interacting tumor cells to extracellular-matrix degradation and derive convergence and invasion-time results.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive asymptotic ECM behavior, transition-probability bounds, convergence results, and closed-form invasion-time probabilities in one-dimensional settings.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is mathematical analysis and simulation of a model, not validation against tumor experiments or patient data; the closed-form invasion results are restricted to one dimension.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct tumor-invasion and cell-microenvironment relevance; formal stochastic/dynamical analysis and numerical simulation checks.

sections.title: Ventilation Perfusion Functional Difference Images in Lung SPECT: a linear and symmetrical scale as an alternative to the Ventilation Perfusion Ratio
sections.abstract: The paper evaluates a bounded, symmetric ventilation–perfusion difference scale as an alternative to ratio images for displaying mismatches in lung SPECT.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose that a relative VQ-difference scale is symmetric and bounded from −1 to +1, and report deriving image thresholds from their patient examples.
sections.unique_caveat: The cohort is ten patients and results are shown for three; diagnostic benefit is proposed rather than established by an external or outcome-based validation study.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Ten-patient investigation; the arXiv record reports an existing Physica Medica 2024 reference and DOI 10.1016/j.ejmp.2024.103306; the arXiv announcement itself is a new submission.

sections.title: Can a self-sustaining chemical network emerge due to just a few catalysts?
sections.abstract: A stochastic mathematical model examines when heterogeneous catalytic activity and reaction compatibility permit reflexively autocatalytic, food-generated chemical networks to form.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors show mathematically that reaction-dependent catalysis can alter classical RAF phase-transition criteria and that heavy-tailed catalytic weights may permit RAF formation even as catalytic intensity tends to zero.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical random-network result; it does not demonstrate that such a network forms in a laboratory or occurs in a prebiotic environment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct relevance to catalytic networks and chemical origins-of-life theory; derived formation/nonformation criteria and a heavy-tailed-weight phase transition.

sections.title: Estimation of Very High Energy Electron (VHEE) beam parameters using an in-air screen
sections.abstract: The authors develop a scattering-corrected method for estimating very-high-energy electron beam parameters from quadrupole scans and in-air screen measurements, motivated by radiotherapy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a multiple-scattering correction that recovers simulated beam parameters and yields experimental estimates within expected ranges after fitting correction factors.
sections.unique_caveat: The study concerns accelerator beam characterization, not patient treatment or clinical outcomes; the authors call for more work to improve consistency and reliability of experimental estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Monte Carlo validation and measurements at the PEER end station; abstract reports parameter errors and experimental emittance ranges.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Computational representations: CellCanon and the protein-backbone model apply different learned/mathematical approaches, not independent biological validation. Cell-history-aware expression modeling: the review highlights growth, division, and measurement design. Tumor and chemical-network dynamics: the Cellular Potts and RAF papers are theoretical/modeling studies without direct experimental confirmation. Medical physics: PGTI is phantom-tested, VQ-difference uses a small human cohort, and VHEE measures accelerator beam parameters; validation levels differ.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Prospective, external perturbation-screen tests for CellCanon; independent experimental conformational ensembles and contextual extensions for the protein model; larger heterogeneous phantom and patient cohorts with locked settings for PGTI/VQ-difference; lineage-resolved matched cell-age/size, nascent/mature RNA, and protein measurements to test cell-cycle noise models.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This batch mixes computational models, a review, phantom imaging, and small-cohort imaging. Benchmark and phantom results are promising within their reported settings, but they are not clinical validation or evidence of field-wide popularity.
